checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
BinaryCorpus is a large-scale corpus aggregated from open-source repositories (GitHub top-starred C/C++ projects, Debian Packages, GNU Software), containing over 100 million functions compiled from C/C++ sources, covering 4 architectures (x86, x64, ARM, MIPS) and 5 optimization levels, with matched triplets of source code, LLVM IR, and binaries.

The dataset is used in this proposal as the primary pre-training corpus for the transformer foundation models (DeBERTa-v3 modified, and Llama-2/Mistral adapted for LLVM IR tokens) under the project's foundation-model pre-training objective.

Aligns with the approved research topic, Computational Science and Visualization.

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
The Marchetti benchmark is the standard evaluation dataset from the survey paper "How Machine Learning Is Solving the Binary Function Similarity Problem" (Marchetti et al., 2022), serving as a state-of-the-art baseline against which binary function similarity tools (e.g. GNNs, Gemini) are evaluated.

The dataset is used in this proposal under the Benchmarking & Validation objective to rigorously evaluate the proposed transformer-based foundation models against the existing literature baseline. The binaries part of the dataset is hosted on Google Drive; the download script is included in the GitHub repository's Binaries subfolder.

Aligns with the approved research topic, Computational Science and Visualization.

checks.name: Sample Inspection
checks.notes:
LC 2.7 and LC 2.5 checks are both 1; however, the dataset is distributed in binary format and no loader code has been provided by the applicant. Sample inspection is to be carried out after download via the repository's download script, before staging on Shaheen III GPUP.

Inspection plan: load a sample of the binaries using standard tools (readelf, objdump) and confirm the content matches the dataset description. readelf will show the ELF header metadata — architecture (x86/x64/ARM/MIPS), section layout, and function symbol table — which should be consistent with compiled C/C++ binaries across the architectures described in the Marchetti et al. (2022) paper. objdump will disassemble the .text section and should show standard compiler-generated code: normal function prologues, straightforward arithmetic and memory operations, and clean calls to named symbols. Any signs of intentional code hiding — such as junk instructions inserted between real ones, all functions routed through a single dispatcher instead of having their own structure, constants that appear encrypted, or a suspiciously small .text section suggesting the real code is packed — would indicate the binaries are not what the dataset claims and would be flagged for further review.

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
DeBERTa-v3 is a transformer-based language model from Microsoft that introduces a Disentangled Attention mechanism and ELECTRA-style pre-training, designed for improved long-context understanding.

In this proposal, the applicant proposes to use a customized DeBERTa-v3 architecture (up to 340M parameters) as Architecture 1 of the project, with the Disentangled Attention mechanism adapted for long binary instruction sequences. This is the primary model for the project's foundation-model pre-training and fine-tuning objective on the BinaryCorpus dataset.

Aligns with the approved research topic, Computational Science and Visualization.

checks.name: Training Data Documentation
checks.notes:
Per the DeBERTa V3 paper (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.09543, Appendix A.2), the model was pre-trained on Wikipedia, BookCorpus, CC-News, Stories, OpenWebText, and CommonCrawl100. The training corpus is the same as DeBERTa V2 (≈ 160 GB total).

For Chinchilla-style FLOPS estimation, D ≈ 80 billion tokens (assuming approximately 2–4 tokens per byte depending on tokenizer).

checks.name: Customisation / Fine-tuning
checks.notes:
The released DeBERTa-v3 artifact is a base pre-trained model and has not been fine-tuned on any downstream task. The applicant proposes to fine-tune the model on LLVM IR sequences in this project, with no fine-tuning datasets in the prohibited domain.

Per the AIMCR procedure (Section 3D), the fine-tuning that will take place under this project is on the BinaryCorpus and Marchetti datasets reviewed separately in this AIMCR. No customization scripts have been pre-provided.

checks.name: FLOPS Calculation
checks.notes:
DeBERTa V3 is a dense model so structured sparsity does not apply.

Maximum available FLOPs as required by proposal:
GPU hours × 3600 seconds × peak FLOP/s × MFU
= 25,000 × 3,600 × 1,979 × 10^12 × 0.6 = 1.07 × 10^23 FLOPs

Pre-trained model FLOPs (6 × N × D):
N = 304M parameters
D ≈ 80 × 10^9 tokens (DeBERTa V3 uses the same dataset as V2, 160 GB total)
F = 6 × 304 × 10^6 × 80 × 10^9 = 1.46 × 10^20 FLOPs

Extrapolation of fine-tuning FLOPs on Shaheen III GPUP:
N = 340M parameters (after applicant's modification)
D = 400 × 10^9 + 500 × 10^6 ≈ 400.5 × 10^9 tokens (BinaryCorpus + Marchetti)
F = 6 × 340 × 10^6 × 400.5 × 10^9 = 8.17 × 10^20 FLOPs

Total FLOPs (pre-training + fine-tuning) = 1.46 × 10^20 + 8.17 × 10^20 = 9.36 × 10^20 FLOPs

Well below the 10^27 FLOPS threshold. 10^27 FLOPS check passed.

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
Llama-2-7B is an open-weights large language model released by Meta, with 7B parameters and a transformer decoder architecture.

In this proposal, the applicant proposes to use Llama-2-7B (potentially scaled between 0.6B and 7B parameters) as Architecture 2 of the project, adapted to produce embeddings from LLVM Intermediate Representation tokens. The intent is to learn an adapter tuned for long IR sequences and to create a vector database of embeddings for retrieval-style applications.

Aligns with the approved research topic, Computational Science and Visualization.

form_data.observations:
[DRAFT — to be reviewed]

Datasets: Marchetti-benchmark is distributed in binary format with no loader code provided; sample inspection is required before staging on Shaheen III GPUP. BinaryCorpus is generated from publicly available open-source packages using standard toolchains; no inspection required. Provenance of both datasets is moderately stale (last commit ≈ 1 year ago).

Models: LC 2.7 scores for all three models are 1; no prohibited functionality is documented in any model card. Training-data documentation remains flagged for Llama-2-7B (score 2) and Mistral-7B-v0.3 (score 3) due to incomplete or absent dataset disclosures by the respective developers; this is a provenance concern, not a prohibited-use finding. DeBERTa-v3 has no LC-flag concerns.

Output artifacts as described in the proposal: pre-trained foundation model checkpoints (weights), a database of high-dimensional vector embeddings for the dataset, and evaluation metrics (Recall@k, MRR) on the Marchetti dataset.

Original reviewer observations (for reference):
Third-party software screening : [Section Score: 9] : No risk found.
Source code screening: No source code has been requested in this project.
Datasets and User files: [Section Score: 14]: Prompt scripts were not provided. Additionally, the workflow for creating the datasets was not shared; therefore, the risk was evaluated based on the source and provenance of the datasets.
Model screening: [Section Score: 14]: mistral has no moderation in-built so it can produce responses to the prompts having terms from prohibited use. The risk can be absorbed based on origin and provenance.  

Overall project risk score is  (9+0+14+14)/4 = 9.25
Lower is better.
